unmapped_findings: The 19Al alloy (Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu at.%) has EDS-measured chemical composition Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 at.% (Table 1) and an Archimedes density of 6.66 g·cm^-3 (b0012, b0013, b0017).

Increasing Al content slows the β-Mn precipitation kinetics: for the 19Al alloy the α→β-Mn transformation was complete only after 10 h at 550 °C, but at 600 °C and above the α had almost completely transformed into β-Mn after just 1 h of aging (b0053).

The optimal aging temperature range for achieving ultra-high hardness (resolvable from the hardness contour maps) increases with Al content: ~525–600 °C for 15Al, ~550–600 °C for 17Al and ~575–625 °C for 19Al (b0038).

The 19Al solution-treated baseline hardness is 263.8 ± 1.1 HV, and its overall aged hardness window spans 263.8 HV to 917.8 HV (Table 4); the 19Al peak of 917.8 ± 24.5 HV occurred after aging at 600 °C for 10 h, i.e. a different condition from this 600 °C/1 h sample (b0031, b0032).
